newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - Lomu not expected back until September.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Lomu not expected back until September.

text.p: Star winger Jonah Lomu's return to rugby will be later rather than sooner, according to his manager Phil Kingsley-Jones.
In Wellington's Dominion newspaper on Wednesday, Kingsley-Jones said speculation that Lomu could be back playing by July was unrealistic.
The manager believed Lomu won't be playing again until at least September, even though he's fitter than ever.
"We don't know yet how long it'll take the powerful steroid drugs he's taking to pass through his system," Kingsley-Jones told the newspaper.
"He can only return when there is absolute confidence he can pass any test."
It would not be known whether Lomu had fully recovered from his acute kidney illness until his treatment had ended in July.
Lomu was forced out of the game early this year by the illness, with predictions that he'd be back playing rugby in six months.
"I can tell you Jonah's jumping out of his skin and he has never been fitter," Kingsley-Jones said.
"He could play tomorrow. He's really missing his rugby."

The hefty winger has been in demand internationally, having been a guest commentator at the sevens World Cup in Hong Kong and at the Japan sevens. He has a similar role to fulfil in France next month.
